methodological_questions: How to define a shaper in the available data?
How to measure whether a role 'travels better' (e.g., signature Delta, portability metric)?
What threshold separates cut-heavy from drive-heavy?
How to avoid lookahead bias when classifying players by pre-move play-type shares?
What controls for destination team context are needed?
How to deal with the small sample of shaper movers (n=24)?
How robust is the portability metric to play-type labeling errors?
What confounders (team quality, role change, usage) could drive spurious differences?

historical_evidence.finding: Pre-move cut share (vs drive share) predicts whether a connector's organizational function reproduces after a move. Cut share rho=+0.265 p=0.011 AUC 0.653; cut-drive rho=+0.314 p=0.002 AUC 0.656; drive rho=-0.278 p=0.007. Top cut tercile 65% portable median Delta +0.167, bottom 35% median -0.039. LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005. n=92 connector movers.

A mover's displacement signature is more similar across franchises than profile-matched destination decoys' signatures: median Delta=+0.0557, perm p=0.0050, 173/294=58.8% positive, sign p=2.87e-3, dest-fr CI [+0.0192,+0.0859]. Confirms that role signatures are portable.

DRIVE PPP is materially higher in regular season (1.198) than playoffs (0.912), a drop of 0.286 across 25 teams, suggesting drive-based effectiveness is less stable or transferable to higher-intensity settings.

Play-type labeling audit found OTHER possessions end in fouls 36% of the time (inflating PPP), while DRIVE is 12pp below a foul benchmark (foul leakage). Only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type. Systematic labeling bias exists for drive and cut play types.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attempt to compare DRIVE-as-BEST PPP against constrained baseline with n=44
failed_approaches.why: Observed gap -0.066 is below MDE 0.180; n=44 cannot distinguish a true null from an effect up to 0.18 PPP. Risk SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER made the test unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring play-type memory (lag-1 effect ≥ lag-2) to define persistent impact
failed_approaches.why: Flat non-decaying lifts collapse under within-team baseline; team-quality confound. Risk CONFOUNDING produced artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Checking portability median Delta robustness to pairing rule
failed_approaches.why: Menu-similarity confound left organizer-connector gap CI including 0 after correction. Small sample and confounding limited inference.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring decision-quality hit rate of engine top play-type vs team modal
failed_approaches.why: Leakage/lookahead bias inflated the result; the apparently high hit rate was an artifact of how the comparison was constructed.

evidence_establishes: Earlier direct work (SF-CHT-057) found that pre-move cut share positively predicts connector portability while drive share negatively predicts it, in 92 connector movers, with effect sizes large enough to be detectable (though with small-sample limitations).
Signature portability is confirmed: displacement signatures travel across team contexts better than decoy signatures (SF19).
DRIVE-based efficiency is markedly reduced in higher-stakes contexts (playoff drop, APPS-011), which may contribute to poorer travel for drive-heavy players.
Play-type labels (cut, drive, OTHER) carry systematic artifacts (foul leakage, initiation_type mismatch) that can bias any share-based classification of players (CHT-025).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the cut-vs-drive portability difference holds specifically for 'shapers' as opposed to the broader 'connector' class.
Whether the relationship is causal or confounded by team-quality rosters, role continuity, or usage differences.
Whether the effect can be estimated with adequate power in the current dataset, given only n=24 suitable units.
That drive-heavy roles always travel worse; SF-APPS-011 shows drop in playoffs but not necessarily across all team transitions.
own_inferences: With only 24 eligible shaper-movers in 2022–26, the study is severely underpowered to detect the portability differences observed in the earlier 92-mover sample; the MDE would be at least as large as the effect sizes reported, likely making the test inconclusive.
The classification of 'shaper' is not operationally defined in the task; it likely overlaps with the connector concept used in prior work, but may be narrower, further reducing the effective sample.
Any threshold splitting cut-heavy from drive-heavy will be arbitrary and sensitive to play-type labeling noise (especially given the OTHER-foul and DRIVE-leak issues).
Even if a positive signal were found, the risk of confounding by team context and role change would be acute with so few units.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'shaper' and how it relates to the 'connector' class used in prior work.
Which portability metric 'travel better' refers to (the earlier studies used Delta signature similarity; other metrics could be used).
The true distribution of cut and drive shares among shaper movers in 2022–26 and whether it provides sufficient contrast.
Whether the prior result (SF-CHT-057) would replicate in a completely independent, later-season sample after correcting for known labeling biases.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence directly tested a very similar hypothesis (cut- vs. drive-based portability for connectors) and found a supported positive result. This does not change the decision to recommend against a new small-sample test, because the earlier work already partially answered the question and the even smaller n=24 in the current setting makes a convincing independent test infeasible.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 24 shaper-mover units are available; to detect an effect of the magnitude seen in SF-CHT-057 (median Delta gap ~0.206 between top and bottom cut terciles) with 80% power would likely require over 50-100 units, so power will be far below conventional thresholds.
The number of cut-heavy or drive-heavy shapers may be extremely small once a reasonable shaper definition and threshold are applied, making meaningful comparison impossible.
Team quality, role continuity, and usage are strong confounders; with only 24 units, adequate covariate adjustment is impossible and residual confounding could easily produce spurious direction.

Play-type labels that form the basis of cut/drive classification are known to have systematic biases (CHT-025 foul leakage, initiation_type gaps), so the exposure variable itself is measured with error.

prior_work.summary: Study family SF-CHT-057 tested a near-identical hypothesis on connector movers (n=92) and found that pre-move cut share positively predicts portability while drive share negatively predicts it (supported, though with small-sample risk). This direct prior work already establishes a positive signal for a closely related construct. The current question narrows to 'shapers' with only n=24 units, making the remaining uncertainty about precision and shaper-specific generalizability rather than a completely open question.

risks.text: With n=24, the study will be unable to distinguish a true effect of plausible size from a null; the minimal detectable effect will exceed the observed gaps from prior work.
The number of cut-heavy shapers (or drive-heavy) may be very small, yielding an uninformative comparison even at the full sample.
Team context, roster quality, coaching style, and player role change all confound the relationship between pre-move play-type mix and subsequent portability.
Play-type assignment errors (particularly OTHER foul inflation and DRIVE foul leakage) reduce the reliability of cut/drive share as an exposure.
Classifying players as shapers or cut-heavy using future data (e.g., using the entire 2022-26 window for a mover who moved in 2024) would produce artificial information leakage.
Players who change teams may be selected on extreme prior performance, causing regression-to-the-mean effects that could spuriously indicate better or worse travel.

design.estimand: Difference in median portability Delta (pre-to-post signature similarity above profile-matched decoys) between shapers classified as cut-heavy (top tercile of pre-move cut share among shapers) and drive-heavy (bottom tercile or top tercile of drive share).
design.unit: Player-move (a shaper who changed teams between 2022-23 and 2025-26 seasons).
design.sample: All identified shaper movers in the 2022-23 through 2025-26 data windows (n=24 as recorded). Pre-move classification uses only data from the season (or two seasons) before the move, without using any post-move data.
design.power: Below 30% for an effect size of Delta gap ~0.20 (the tercile gap observed in SF-CHT-057). The MDE at 80% power given 24 units and estimated dispersion would be >0.35 Delta units, which is unrealistically large.
design.controls: Destination-team offensive rating in the first post-move season, pre-move usage rate, position, and a simple indicator of roster continuity (e.g., returning starters) to partially address confounding.
design.falsification: Apply the same cut/drive classification to a set of non-movers (players who stayed with the same team) matched on usage and position, and verify that the portability differential does not appear among non-movers.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary contrast (cut-heavy vs. drive-heavy median Delta) with an exact rank-based permutation test.
design.decision_rule: One-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test with alpha=0.05. Declare support if permutation p < 0.05 and the direction matches the hypothesis (cut-heavy > drive-heavy). Require a minimum of 5 cut-heavy and 5 drive-heavy shapers to run the test; otherwise declare the study untestable.
design.data_version: NBA play-by-play and derived play-type records through 2025-26 season end (2026-06-21), using the V4 engine play-type mapping and the signature/decoy portability framework from SF19.

methodological_questions: How to define cut-heavy vs drive-heavy shapers?
How to measure whether a role travels better?
How to quantify role portability across teams?
How to avoid lookahead bias in classifying players?
What controls for team context are necessary?
What sample size is needed for player-level comparisons?
How to handle player role changes over time?
What metrics capture role consistency?
args.query: Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.
